author: @akraminabdullah
comment:
So I've been using this phone for 3 months now, and yeah I totally love it. I was an iPhone user, which the last phone I used is the 15 Pro Max. Everything is great to me, but there's a few aesterisks though. Selfie and 0.7x ultra wide is ok, and I don't use those much. Compared to the main and 5x periscope, those camera has insane quality. Rear display really make me love taking selfies with the back camera. I still think that videos are better on iPhones, but this phone's video quality is just as good. Super steady shot, for example, is really steady on straight movements, but struggles a bit at orbit pan shots. Perfomance is great, I never had overheating thanks to it's large vapour chamber. Games however, iPhones are more optimized for that, for example especially supercell games — my iPhone 11 Pro also runs 60hz like my 15 PM and Xiaomi. Haptics are objective in my opinion — they're much stronger with the Xiaomi, but I hope that there are more haptic patterns like what we take for granted in iPhones. Speakers are loud. Display is very smooth and rarely stutters. I'm using the Chinese ver btw. Yes, it's a little difficult to use it, but I just get used to it and have minimal problems personally

Will I recommend the Xiaomi? It's not that easy of a recommendation, but I totally am happy having this one over the iPhone. There are also very few people that uses the Xiaomi at my region, and everyone are just impressed of the Xiaomi. If you're reading this far, thank you — I very rarely make comments

author: @Sweet-Vermouth
comment:
For those wondering how this works, this is an oversimplified version - 
Each pixel has 3 photo-diodes each sensitive to different colors of light (RGB). When you open your camera, a voltage is applied across every diode. In the dark very little current is allowed to pass through the diode. The more light falls on the photo-diode, the more current it allows to pass through it. If a very bright light falls on the diode, a lot of current passes through the diode causing it to burn out and permanently allow current to pass through. 
If the camera is not on, there is no voltage across the diode so no current will flow through it when bright light shines on it. The sensor will not be affected if the camera is not on.

I am a bookkeeper with a technical mind but I am also an educator.
